newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan aluminium demand outlook dull--federation.
newsitem.headline: Japan aluminium demand outlook dull--federation.

text.p: The outlook for Japan's aluminium demand remains lacklustre despite record levels of output and shipments in July and strong year-on-year gains in August as well, Japan Aluminium Federation officials said on Thursday.

"At present, consumption has no sustainability," said Masahiro Kumamoto, chairman of the federation and president of Kobe Steel Ltd, at a news conference announcing Japan's August aluminium mill output and shipments.
His view was echoed by Akira Fujii, vice chairman of the federation and president of Mitsubishi Aluminum Co.
"It'd be great for us if it continued like this, but there are various reasons it probably won't," he said. "The economy is slow to recover."

Japan's August output of both flat-rolled and extruded aluminium products registered double-digit year-on-year growth, while shipments rose more modestly. The August figures were down, however, from July's record levels.

Federation officials attributed the growth to strong demand for beverage can sheet during unusually hot weather in July and early August, as well as healthy demand from aluminium sash manufacturers as consumers rushed to purchase homes ahead of next April's scheduled increase in Japan's consumption tax.
